messages.subject: Extrapolating data
parts:
Dear Distancer's 

Please pardon my lack of in-depth knowledge on the software, I am very much new to this and just trying to teach myself the ways. 

I am trying to produce population estimates for Grant's Gazelle within a Kenyan conservancy. I have 8 transects, at 2km each, which are split into 4 woodland and 4 plains habitats, I have produced population estimates of the area covered by sampling effort. The sampled area size was in hectares, the effort is in Km^2 (Transect length x number of time sampled). What I want to do now, is extrapolate the data to be representative of the habitats conservancy-wide. 

The area sampled for plains had approx. 188.57 indvs Lower confidence limit, 193.59 indvs for the estimate and 206.27 indvs upper confidence limit. 
To extrapolate I understand I will need the density value p = 0.7 for unit area used (which is KM^2?) and the total area covered by,  in this case, plains. Which is 6394ha. What I am not sure is how to use the density value. Do I just include another column with this value?

Area Area Size (ha)  Plains Transect Effort Herbivores     Total Distance (m) Compass Bearing  Density (?)
Naboisho          6394   Balanite                   138 Grant Gazelle    1 450                    1                        0.7
Naboisho          6394    Balanite                   138 Grant Gazelle         1 82                         1                         0.7

Best wishes, 

Oli Barnes

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Extrapolating data
parts:
Hi Oli

Afraid I don't quite follow you.

I've re-imported your plains data (except for the observation that had a bearing of 399 degrees !?) to understand your data.

In your data file, you note the Region area of 1112ha.  However at the end of your message, you state the total area of plains is 6394ha.

It is customary in distance sampling for the Region area to be the size of the area about which you wish to make inference (which is also the area where your transects might have been placed).  Why did you not simply enter 6394 in your dataset?  What extrapolation are you referring to?

The distribution of detection distances seems reasonable.  Your inference will be a bit hampered by the small number of replicate transects (4).

If the answer is complicated, perhaps we should discuss off-list and report our finding back to the list when we straighten this out.
